name: Post-validation Peer-review Dialogue Plan
title: Post-validation Dialogue

questions.help: Describe what you understood the exposé to be trying to do. There is no required wording.
questions.text: Thinking about the exposé you reviewed, how would you describe its main aim in your own words?
questions.completeWhen: The answer describes the exposé's main aim, problem, claim, or focus as the participant understood it.
questions.evidenceGoal: The participant explains their understanding of the reviewed work.
questions.followUpDirection: If the main aim is unclear, ask what the exposé was mainly trying to do or address.

questions.help: Choose any judgment from your review and explain what standard or quality you were looking for.
questions.text: Think of one judgment you made in your review. What standard or criterion were you using when you made it?
questions.completeWhen: The answer identifies at least one standard or criterion used to make a judgment about the exposé.
questions.evidenceGoal: The participant explains a criterion or quality standard behind one of their judgments.
questions.followUpDirection: If the standard is unclear, ask what quality or standard the participant was comparing the work against.

questions.help: Explain what you noticed in the exposé that led to the comment.
questions.text: Thinking about your review, choose one comment you made. What in the exposé led you to make that comment?
questions.anchoredText: In your review, you wrote: “{{anchor}}” What in the exposé led you to write this feedback?
questions.completeWhen: The answer identifies a concrete feature, passage, claim, evidence, omission, wording, or other aspect of the exposé that led to the comment.
questions.evidenceGoal: The participant connects submitted feedback to evidence or features in the reviewed exposé.
questions.followUpDirection: If the connection is unclear, ask which specific part or feature of the exposé led to the comment.

questions.help: Explain the reason behind the point and why it mattered for the exposé.
questions.text: Thinking about your review, choose one important point you made. If the author asked why you made that point, what would you say?
questions.anchoredText: In your review, you wrote: “{{anchor}}” If the author asked why you made this point, what would you say?
questions.completeWhen: The answer gives a reason for the review point and explains why it mattered for the exposé.
questions.evidenceGoal: The participant explains and justifies a review judgment and can articulate it from the author's perspective.
questions.followUpDirection: If the reason is unclear, ask what made the point important or what the participant would say to explain it to the author.

questions.help: Name one suggestion from your review and explain the change you expected it to produce.
questions.text: Thinking about your review, choose one suggestion you made. What change did you expect it to make to the exposé?
questions.completeWhen: The answer identifies a concrete expected change or consequence of the suggestion.
questions.evidenceGoal: The participant explains the intended effect of a suggestion in their feedback.
questions.followUpDirection: If the expected effect is unclear, ask what the participant expected to change if the author followed the suggestion.

questions.help: If there was something you were unsure about, explain it. If not, you can say that.
questions.text: Thinking about your review, was there anything you were unsure about? If so, what made you unsure?
questions.completeWhen: The answer identifies an uncertainty, assumption, missing information, alternative interpretation, or limitation, or clearly states that there was no meaningful uncertainty.
questions.evidenceGoal: The participant identifies uncertainty, assumptions, or limits in their own judgment, or clearly states that none were salient.
questions.followUpDirection: If uncertainty is mentioned but unclear, ask what made that point uncertain. If the participant clearly reports no uncertainty, do not probe further.

questions.help: Describe how you chose which issues were worth including in your review.
questions.text: Thinking about your review, how did you decide which points to focus on?
questions.completeWhen: The answer explains how the participant selected or prioritized points for the review.
questions.evidenceGoal: The participant explains their review strategy and prioritization.
questions.followUpDirection: If the selection strategy is unclear, ask how the participant chose between several possible points.

categories.label: Understanding the reviewed work
categories.evidenceGoal: The participant explains what they understood the reviewed exposé to be trying to do.

categories.label: Criteria used for judgment
categories.evidenceGoal: The participant explains the standard or criterion used to judge quality.

categories.label: Evidence grounding
categories.evidenceGoal: The participant connects submitted feedback to evidence or features in the reviewed exposé.

categories.label: Judgment justification and challenge
categories.evidenceGoal: The participant explains and justifies a review judgment and can articulate it from the author's perspective.

categories.label: Constructive implications
categories.evidenceGoal: The participant explains the intended effect of a suggestion in their feedback.

categories.label: Assumptions, uncertainty, and limits
categories.evidenceGoal: The participant identifies assumptions, uncertainty, or limits in their own review, or clearly states that none were salient.

categories.label: Review strategy and reflection
categories.evidenceGoal: The participant explains how they selected priorities and approached the review.
categories.sourceCategory: Socratic questions about the question and reflection

description: Adaptive post-validation dialogue covering seven peer-review reasoning categories for one review.
completionMessage: Thank you. The dialogue is complete.
